title: Risk Definition
equation: Risk = Σ [P(load) × P(adverse response | load) × Consequences]

P(load).description: Annual probability of the loading event (flood, earthquake)

P(adverse response).description: Conditional probability of dam failure given the load

Consequences.description: Expected consequences if failure occurs (life loss, economic damage)

applicability: Summation over all load levels and all failure modes. For a single PFM: Risk = P(failure) × C(failure). Annualized risk = sum across all PFMs.

title: Annualized Failure Probability (AFP)

AFP.description: Total annual probability of dam failure from all load categories

P(load_i).description: Annual probability of load level i

P(failure|load_i).description: Conditional probability of failure given load level i (system response probability)

applicability: Integrate over all load levels: flood (IDF to PMF), seismic (OBE to MCE), and normal (sunny-day failures). Compare AFP to tolerable risk thresholds (USBR/USACE: 10⁻⁴/yr).
source: USBR Dam Safety Risk Analysis Best Practices

title: Annualized Life Loss

ALL.description: Average expected life loss per year from dam failure

P(failure_j).description: Annual probability of failure mode j

LL_j.description: Expected life loss if failure mode j occurs

applicability: ALL integrates over all failure modes and load levels. USACE guideline: if ALL > 0.001 lives/year, risk reduction measures should be considered. USBR uses f-N charts plotting AFP vs. expected life loss.

title: Life Loss Estimation (RCEM Simplified)

PAR.description: Population at risk in the inundation zone

FR.description: Fatality rate (function of flood severity, warning time, understanding)

applicability: RCEM (Reclamation Consequence Estimating Methodology) provides fatality rate curves. Key inputs: DV product (depth × velocity), flood depth, warning time, time of day, understanding of threat. Typical FR: 0.01 (good warning, low severity) to 0.50+ (no warning, high severity).

title: Flood Severity Index — DV Product
applicability: DV < 0.5 m²/s: low severity (wading possible). DV 0.5–2: moderate (vehicles swept). DV 2–7: high severity (structural damage). DV > 7: extreme (complete destruction). Used with RCEM fatality rate tables and dam breach inundation modeling.

title: Critical Gradient for Internal Erosion Initiation

i_cr.description: Critical hydraulic gradient for piping initiation (upward flow)

G_s.description: Specific gravity of soil particles (2.65 typical)

applicability: For upward seepage (heaving/boiling at downstream toe). i_cr ≈ 1.0 for typical soils. For horizontal BEP: Sellmeijer equation gives critical gradient considering grain size, thickness, and aquifer permeability. FS against piping = i_cr / i_actual ≥ 2.0–3.0 depending on agency.

title: Event Tree Probability — Sequential Events

P(path).description: Probability of a specific failure path

P(eventₙ).description: Conditional probability of each event in the chain

applicability: Event tree for internal erosion: P(initiation) × P(continuation) × P(progression) × P(unsuccessful detection/intervention) × P(breach). Each node estimated by expert elicitation, analysis, or historical data. Sum of all paths = total failure probability for that PFM.
source: USBR Best Practices in Dam Safety Risk Analysis

title: Adjusted Cost per Statistical Life Saved (ACSLS)
equation: ACSLS = (Annualized cost of risk reduction) / (Reduction in ALL)

ACSLS.description: Cost per statistical life saved — measure of cost-effectiveness

Annualized cost.description: Annual equivalent cost of the dam modification (capital + O&M)

Reduction in ALL.description: Decrease in Annualized Life Loss from the modification

applicability: Used to evaluate whether a risk reduction measure is cost-effective. USACE guideline: modifications with ACSLS < $7–15 million/life are generally justifiable (comparable to other life-safety investments). Higher ACSLS may still be justified in ALARP zone.
